title: Audit every repository-owned guard against its opposite failure direction, and instrument the two highest-value gaps
rebase_note: main moved from 5a3fb24 to 96b2cb8 (PR #74, stranded Level-2 evaluation records) while this slice was in flight. Rebased: agent-state/progress.md was reconstructed as main's blob VERBATIM as the prefix (sha256 dd59066f89d0b0da, byte-identical) plus this slice's own 14671-byte block, and this contract was taken wholesale. No file that main touched was otherwise altered.
objective: Every guard has two failure directions - wrongly ACCEPT (it misses the thing it exists to catch) and wrongly REJECT (it fires on correct work). This repository instruments the direction that motivated each guard and, in several cases, only that one. Enumerate the guards this repository OWNS by searching the tree, state both directions for each, MEASURE which direction is actually tested rather than inferring it from a test name, add the missing direction for the highest-value gaps, and file the rest as reasoned follow-ups.
materiality: Test and guard quality only. Zero change to application behaviour, zero change to any published claim, verdict, quota or classification.

measured_premise.claim: The false-alarm direction (wrongly REJECT) is under-instrumented relative to the false-accept direction, and it is the more expensive of the two because it damages the instrument's standing rather than the artefact.
measured_premise.how_the_guard_list_was_derived: By searching the tree (git grep / git ls-files over scripts, tests, tests/support, .github, apps/api/app), never from the dispatch brief's example list. A list in a brief goes stale; deriving it is the only way to see a guard the brief does not name.
measured_premise.measured_baseline: python -m pytest -q on the base commit with DATABASE_URL unset: 2426 passed, 244 skipped. This independently reproduces the figure recorded in the previous handoff (2426 / 244 without Postgres), so two derivations agree.

in_scope: A full inventory of repository-owned guards with BOTH failure directions stated for each, and the tested/untested status of each direction MEASURED by reading the assertions, not the test names.

GAP 1 - scripts/check_urls.py (the URL host allowlist / disclosure guard) has ZERO tests in EITHER direction. Add tests/unit/test_url_allowlist.py covering both: the false-alarm direction (a legitimate, allowlisted host must never be rejected; the committed tree must stay green; a redaction marker must remain committable; --list must never fail a build) and the missed-leak direction (an unlisted host fails with exit 1; lockfile resolved URLs are in scope; a lookalike domain is not swallowed by a suffix rule; userinfo cannot disguise the real host).

GAP 1b - the two structural blind spots measured in check_urls.py (a JSON-escaped 'https:\/\/' authority is not matched by URL_RE; a file with a NUL byte in its first 8192 bytes is skipped whole, which a UTF-16 encoded text file would trigger) are converted from SILENT holes into MONITORED ones: pinned as the documented limits they are, plus an assertion that no tracked TEXT file currently exercises either. Scoped to text-suffixed files deliberately, so that adding a legitimate binary asset does not red the build - that would be the very false alarm this slice exists to prevent.

GAP 2 - tests/unit/test_adviser_no_llm_import.py has NO positive control: nothing in the repository demonstrates that its probe is capable of detecting a leak at all. Add a positive control that runs the identical probe shape against a module measured to import the LLM package (app.adviser.router, measured: 7 leaked modules) and requires it to REPORT the leak, plus a probe-list integrity assertion so a rename cannot silently empty the guard.

GAP 2b - the probe's module list has drifted behind the deterministic adviser core. Four core modules (explain, portability, quota_math, export) were never probed; all four measured clean, so adding them is a strict strengthening with a measured-zero risk of reddening.
out_of_scope_zero_diff: agent-state/feature_list.json - byte-identical, blob 154de1fef2ba20f587c9ec2d1302ebe2bfb5bfa1. No feature flag flips.

tests/support/source_scan.py (blob 3a86f03aeb17) and tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py (blob 183619e00375) - audited and reported on, never edited. If either goes red, that is reported rather than repaired.
apps/web/package-lock.json (blob 98f786c2bb0d) - untouched; every resolved URL stays on the public registry.

.github/workflows/ci.yml (blob 4f80c771f956) and scripts/check.ps1 (blob f68e2b972997) - two other builders hold these concurrently. Not edited. scripts/check.sh (blob 4543d6f11eab) left alone for symmetry.

scripts/check_urls.py itself - the measured blind spots are REPORTED and PINNED, never repaired here. Repairing a guard's matching rules is a behaviour change to a security control and needs owner approval; and a guard that cannot hold both directions is a finding, not something to trade away.
Every application module: no change to ingest, classify, publish, read_api or adviser behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: The guard inventory is derived by searching the tree and names every repository-owned guard found, each with an explicit wrongly-ACCEPT and wrongly-REJECT statement.
For every guard, the tested/untested status of each direction is established by reading what the test ASSERTS, and any case where a test name overstates its assertion is reported.
tests/unit/test_url_allowlist.py exists and covers both directions of the URL host allowlist guard.
tests/unit/test_adviser_no_llm_import.py gains a positive control proving its probe can detect a leak.

EVERY added test is proven non-vacuous by mutation: baseline GREEN, the guarded thing broken, test RED, file restored byte-exactly and restoration PROVED by git hash-object (never by git diff --numstat).
Every mutation prints the patched line and asserts its anchor matched EXACTLY ONCE, so a mutation that does not apply cannot be mistaken for a control that does not fire.
No existing guard is weakened. Full suite passes at or above the 2426-passed baseline.
No internal package-feed hostname or credential appears in any file, report, commit message or PR body.
verification_commands: git hash-object <each protected path> compared against the recorded pre-change blob
negative_and_regression_tests: Mutation M1: break the suffix rule in is_allowed so a lookalike domain matches - the lookalike test must go RED.
Mutation M2: break userinfo stripping in normalise_host - the userinfo-disguise test must go RED.
Mutation M3: make main() return 0 on violations - the end-to-end unlisted-host test must go RED.

Mutation M4: break the leak predicate inside the adviser probe - the NEW positive control must go RED while the ORIGINAL test stays GREEN, which is the direct demonstration that the original was incapable.
Mutation M5: point the probe list at a module that does not exist - the probe-list integrity test must go RED.
Regression: full suite, plus the untouched secrets-baseline and route-guard suites.

data_security_privacy_portability_z0.data: None. No migration, no schema change, no catalogue record touched.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.security: Positive. The disclosure guard that keeps internal hostnames out of a public repository gains its first tests, and two structural blind spots in it become monitored instead of silent.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.privacy: No secret, token, credential or internal hostname is read, printed or committed. The new tests use RFC 2606 reserved names only.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.portability: None. Standard library plus pytest; no new dependency, no network, no database.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.z0: No Z0 rule, quota or classification is read or changed.

evaluation_level_rationale: Level 2. The work changes the repository's security-boundary instrumentation (the disclosure guard) and asserts claims about what other guards do and do not catch. A claim about a guard's capability is exactly the kind of claim that reads true and measures false, so it needs an adversarial fresh-context check.
boundary: Draft PR only. Do not merge. Do not flip any ledger flag. agent-state/feature_list.json stays byte-identical and F001 keeps its existing state.
